title: Tax on NRE Deposit Interest: Key Rules for NRIs
description: Interest earned on Non-Resident External (NRE) accounts in India is fully exempt from income tax in India for Non-Resident Indians (NRIs). This tax exemption .

faq.q: What is the primary benefit of an NRE account for NRIs?
faq.a: The primary benefit is that the interest earned on deposits in an NRE account is completely exempt from income tax in India, and both the principal and interest are fully repatriable.

faq.q: Can I deposit my Indian earnings into an NRE account?
faq.a: No, NRE accounts are specifically for depositing foreign earnings. Any income earned in India, such as rental income or salary, should be deposited into an NRO account.

faq.q: Is interest from NRE savings accounts also tax-exempt?
faq.a: Yes, the tax exemption under Section 10(4)(ii) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, applies to interest earned on both NRE savings accounts and NRE fixed deposits.

faq.q: Are NRE account funds freely repatriable?
faq.a: Yes, both the principal amount and the interest earned in an NRE account are fully and freely repatriable to your overseas bank account.

faq.q: Do I need to declare NRE interest income in my Indian tax return?
faq.a: No, since the interest from NRE accounts is exempt from Indian income tax, you do not need to declare it in your Indian income tax return.

faq.q: What happens to my NRE account if I return to India permanently?
faq.a: If you return to India and become a Resident Indian, your NRE account must be converted into a Resident Ordinary (RO) account or a Resident Foreign Currency (RFC) account, depending on the nature of funds. The tax exemption on interest will then cease.
